 Why This Position Stands Out
 Notre Dame has the stronger overall efficiency profile, but the market is asking South Carolina State to absorb a very large number against a home team that has not yet been tested by an opponent with comparable size, length, and depth. Notre Dame’s adjusted offensive and defensive ratings both sit well above South Carolina State’s, and that gap supports a comfortable Irish win. Even so, the spread appears a touch aggressive relative to the projected margin, which leaves room for South Carolina State to stay inside the number if Notre Dame controls the game without extending the lead late.
The under is also live because the projected score lands a few points below the current total consensus. Notre Dame’s offense has been efficient early, but South Carolina State’s profile is built more on pace and volume than half-court shot quality, and that can flatten when a stronger opponent forces longer possessions and tougher looks. If Notre Dame gets out in front, the game script can reduce late scoring pressure and keep the final total closer to the mid-140s than the upper 140s.

 Notre Dame enters with the better scoring efficiency, shooting a higher field goal percentage, a much better three-point rate, and a stronger offensive rating. The Irish also allow fewer points per game and carry a clear edge in defensive efficiency, which is the biggest separator in this matchup. South Carolina State has been productive on the scoreboard early, but its shooting profile is less efficient and its defensive rating is much softer, which makes sustained success against a power-conference opponent harder to project.
South Carolina State’s path is to keep the game faster and lean on extra possessions, but that approach can also create empty trips if the Irish defend cleanly and limit transition chances. Notre Dame’s home setting and efficiency edge point to control of the game, yet the current spread looks more ambitious than the statistical gap alone would suggest. That is why the best value leans toward the underdog side on the spread rather than a straight home win position.
